# @ratmath/complex 0.3.0: full documentation

> Complex and hypercomplex numbers for RatMath: exact complex arithmetic, honest branches, certified complex analysis, quaternions and octonions. From https://ratmath.com/complex/, commit 5735292. Each page ends with a runnable example; in it, PRINT(...) prints.


---

Page: https://ratmath.com/complex/index.html

@ratmath/complex

## Complex numbers that say which branch they took

Exact complex rationals, certified enclosures of everything that is not rational, and elementary functions that report what happens at a branch cut instead of silently picking a side. Quaternions, octonions and the rest of the doubling ladder are here too, exact.

### What is here

Complex numbers with their functions; Möbius maps and the Riemann sphere; complex analysis with proofs (Taylor models, contour integrals, zeros, residues, the gamma and zeta functions); and the Cayley–Dickson numbers. Every phase of the roadmap for this package is built.

### A first program

```js
import { complex, exp, log, sqrt, polar } from "@ratmath/complex";

String(complex("(1 + 2i)/(3 - i)"));     // "1/10 + 7/10i", exactly
String(complex("(1 + i)^8"));            // "16"
String(sqrt("3 + 4i"));                  // "2 + i": exact when the root is rational

String(exp("1 + i"));                    // "1.4686939399 + 2.2873552872i ± 1.7e-21"
String(exp("1 + i", 200).toString(40));  // forty digits, still certified

String(log("-1"));
// on the cut (the negative real axis).  above: 0 + 3.1415926536i ± 1.7e-21;
// below: 0 - 3.1415926536i ± 1.7e-21.  Convention: above
String(log("-1", { side: "below" }));    // "0 - 3.1415926536i ± 1.7e-21"
```

Numbers are written as text (`"3 - 4i"`, `"1/2 + 0.#3i"`), as a pair `complex(3, -4)`, or as anything Core reads. The quaternions and their relatives are a separate entry point, so a program that only wants complex numbers does not load them:

```js
import { quaternion, rotate, fourSquares } from "@ratmath/complex/cayley";

String(quaternion("1 + 2i").mul("j"));   // "j + 2k"
rotate("1 + k", [1, 0, 0]).map(String);  // ["0", "1", "0"]: a quarter turn about z, exactly
fourSquares(2026);                       // [23n, 23n, 22n, 22n]
```

### Four ideas

Exact where the answer is rational. Sums, products, quotients and whole-number powers of complex rationals are complex rationals, and they are computed as such. So is 3+4i​=2+i, and so is any rotation by a rational quaternion.

Enclosed where it is not. e1+i is not rational, so the answer is a small rectangle with rational corners that is proven to contain it. Ask for more bits and the rectangle shrinks. An uncertain input (a rectangle or a disc) gives a rectangle containing every possible value. See [Rectangles and discs](https://ratmath.com/complex/enclosures.html).

Branch cuts are reported. log, roots, powers and the inverse trigonometric functions jump across a cut. When the input is on the cut, or an uncertain input lies across it, the result holds the value on each side and says so; a number is never returned from the wrong side by accident. See [Branches](https://ratmath.com/complex/branches.html).

Whole functions are enclosed too. A [Taylor model](https://ratmath.com/complex/taylor-models.html) is a polynomial with a proven bound on what it leaves out, valid on a whole disc. From it come [contour integrals](https://ratmath.com/complex/contour-integrals.html) as rectangles, the number of [zeros](https://ratmath.com/complex/zeros.html) inside a contour as a proven whole number, [residues](https://ratmath.com/complex/residues.html), and [real integrals](https://ratmath.com/complex/real-integrals.html) with the steps shown. The [zeros of the zeta function](https://ratmath.com/complex/gamma-zeta.html) are found this way, each one proved to lie on the critical line.

Maps of the sphere are exact. A [Möbius map](https://ratmath.com/complex/mobius.html) with complex rational coefficients sends rational points to rational points and circles to circles, exactly, and stereographic projection onto the [Riemann sphere](https://ratmath.com/complex/riemann-sphere.html) is rational too.

### The roadmap

From the [library roadmap](https://github.com/ratmath/ratmath/blob/main/docs/design/library-roadmap.md#3-a-complex-package-ratmathcomplex). All six phases are built.

| Phase | Contents | State |

| 1 | Exact complex rationals, rectangles and discs, polar form, elementary functions with branch reporting | built |

| 2 | Cayley–Dickson numbers, quaternion rotations, integer quaternions | built |

| 3 | Complex Taylor models; contour integrals; argument principle and zero isolation | built |

| 4 | Residues, Laurent series, singularities, real integrals by residues | built |

| 5 | Möbius and conformal maps; graphics hooks | built (pictures in graphics) |

| 6 | Complex gamma and zeta | built |

It builds on Core and on [analytic](https://ratmath.com/analytic/), whose certified real exp, log, sine, cosine and arctangent are the only transcendental ingredients.

### Try it

```js
// Euler's identity, as far as it can be known: exp(iπ) with π enclosed.
const pi = [new Rational("3.14159265358979"), new Rational("3.14159265358980")];
PRINT("exp(i·[π]) =", exp(rect([0, 0], pi)).toString());

// (3 + 4i)/5 is on the unit circle, so every power of it is too, exactly.
const z = complex("3/5 + 4/5i");
PRINT("z^10 =", z.pow(10).toString(), "  |z^10|² =", z.pow(10).norm().toString());

// A function on its cut tells you so.
PRINT("sqrt(-4)  →", sqrt("-4").toString());
PRINT("asin(2)   →", asin("2").toString());

// i^i is real
PRINT("i^i =", pow("i", "i").toString());

// The doubling ladder: what each level gives up
for (const level of [1, 2, 3, 4]) {
  const p = cayleyDickson(level).properties();
  PRINT(p.name.padEnd(16), "commutative:", p.commutative, " associative:", p.associative, " zero divisors:", p.zeroDivisors ? p.zeroDivisors.join(" times ") + " = 0" : "none");
}

// A contour integral, a count of zeros, and the first zero of zeta
PRINT("∮ dz/z round the unit circle =", contourIntegral("1/z", Contour.circle(0, 1)).toString());
PRINT("solutions of e^z = 3z with |z| < 2:", countZeros("exp(z) - 3z", Contour.circle(0, 2)));
const first = zetaZeros(14, 15).zeros[0];
PRINT("first zero of ζ:", first.enclosure.toString(18), "  proved on the critical line:", first.onCriticalLine);
zeta(2).toString(18)
```

Reference

## Everything in the library

Every export of `@ratmath/complex` and of `@ratmath/complex/cayley`. Anything called `z` below is a `Complex`, text, a pair or a real number, and for the functions also a `Rect` or a `Disc`. `bits` is the precision in binary digits and defaults to 64.

### Complex rationals

| Export | What it does |

| complex(re, im) | A Complex from text ("3 - 4i", "(1 + i)^8"), two parts, a [re, im] pair or a real number in any form Core reads. |

| Complex | .re, .im (Core Rationals); add sub mul div neg conj inv pow(n) scale(q); norm() = \|z\|²; exactModulus() and exactSqrt() (null when irrational); equals isZero isReal isImaginary isGaussianInteger; toString toTeX toJSON toNumbers. Complex.parse(text), Complex.from(x), Complex.ZERO ONE I. |

| CQ | The field Q(i) as a RatMath field object, for linalg and structures. |

| ComplexError | Thrown with a code: division-by-zero, branch-cut, branch-point, pole, precision, bad-option, bad-argument, singularity, zero-on-contour, unsupported; and from the cayley entry point no-quotient, not-a-rotation, too-large. |

### Enclosures

| Export | What it does |

| rect(a, b) | rect("1 + 2i") a point; rect([0, 1], [2, 3]) the rectangle [0,1] + i[2,3]; rect(z, radius) the square around z. |

| Rect | .re, .im as { lo, hi }; .real, .imag as Core RationalIntervals; center width height size isPoint; add sub mul div inv neg conj scale timesI pow; contains intersects intersect hull containsZero; corners() split() round(bits) toDisc() normRange(); toString(digits) toJSON(). Rect.from(x), Rect.hull(...items). |

| disc(center, radius) | The closed disc with rational centre and radius. |

| Disc | .center, .radius; add sub mul div inv neg conj scale; contains intersects hull containsZero (decided exactly); toRect(). |

### Polar form

| Export | What it does |

| polar(z, bits) | { modulus, argument, normSquared, exactModulus, exactTurn } for an exact z; the first two are Core RationalIntervals. |

| modulus(z, bits) | \|z\| as a RationalInterval; also for a rectangle or disc. |

| argument(z, bits) | The principal argument in (−π, π] as a RationalInterval. |

| arg(z, options) | The argument as a Branched result, for inputs that may lie across the negative real axis. |

| exactTurn(z) | The angle as a fraction of a full turn when that is rational (a multiple of 1/8), else null. |

| fromPolar(r, theta, bits) | A Rect around reiθ. theta in radians, or { turns: q }. |

| rootsOfUnity(n, bits) | The n-th roots of unity, counter-clockwise from 1; the rational ones exact. |

| roots(z, n, bits) | All n values of the n-th root of an exact z. |

### Functions

| Export | What it does |

| exp sin cos tan sinh cosh tanh | f(z, bits) or f(z, { bits }) returns a Rect. z is exact, a Rect or a Disc. tan and tanh refuse an enclosure that may contain a pole. |

| log(z, options) | A Branched. Cut: the negative real axis. Options { bits, branch: k, side: "above" \| "below" }; branch k adds 2πik. |

| sqrt(z, options), root(z, n, options) | A Branched; exact when the square root is a complex rational. Branch k multiplies by e2πik/n. |

| pow(z, w, options) | zw. Exact for a whole-number w and exact z; a rational w goes through root; otherwise ewlogz. |

| asin acos atanh | Branched; cut on the real axis outside [−1, 1]; sides above, below. |

| atan asinh | Branched; cut on the imaginary axis outside [−i, i]; sides right, left. |

| acosh | Branched; cut on the real axis left of 1; sides above, below. |

| Branched | value (Rect or null), straddles, cut, candidates ([{ side, value }]), convention ({ side, value } for an exact point on the cut, else null), branch; getters rect (throws on the cut) and hull. |

| continueAlong(fn, path, options) | Carry "log", { root: n } or { pow: w } along a polygonal path of exact points: { value, turns, branch, values }. Options bits, branch, about. |

| winding(path, w) | The winding number of a closed polygon about w (default 0), exact. |

| refined(name, z, options) | A Core Refinement: .quick at once, .exact() certified. |

| plan | The phases still to come. |

### Möbius maps and the Riemann sphere

| Export | What it does |

| mobius(a, b, c, d), mobiusFrom(from, to), Mobius | z ↦ (az + b)/(cz + d), exactly: apply, compose, inverse, equals, classify, fixedPoints, isSphereRotation. See Möbius maps. |

| infinity, isInfinity | The point at infinity. |

| crossRatio, concyclic | The invariant of four points; the exact test for lying on one circle or line. |

| circle(c, r2), lineThrough, circleThrough, GCircle | Circles and lines as Hermitian forms, mapped exactly by map(T). |

| toSphere, fromSphere, chordal2 | Stereographic projection, exact. See The Riemann sphere. |

| cayley, halfPlaneToDisc, discAutomorphism, joukowski, regions | Conformal maps of the standard regions. |

| gridImage, sampleGrid | Data for pictures: exact image circles of a grid; sampled values (estimated). |

### Taylor models

| Export | What it does |

| taylorModel(f, disc, opts) | The model of f on a disc: a polynomial and a proven bound on ∣f−P∣ there. f is text in z or a function of one model. Options order (12), bits (96). Refuses (division-by-zero, branch-point, branch-cut, precision) when a hypothesis cannot be shown. |

| CTM | CTM.z(disc, opts), CTM.constant(disc, value, opts); add sub mul div neg inv pow(n) scale(q); .center .radius .order .bits .disc .error .coefficients; at(z) (Rect), range() (Disc), zeroCount(), derivative(radius), integral(a, b), toString(). The package's exp log sqrt root pow sin cos tan sinh cosh tanh gamma rgamma logGamma zeta accept a model and return one. |

### Contours, integrals, zeros

| Export | What it does |

| Contour | Contour.path(points), polygon(points), rectangle(rect), circle(center, radius, { clockwise }), arc(center, from, to, { clockwise }), from(x); .pieces .start .end .closed; join(other) reversed() winding(w) sample(perPiece). |

| contourIntegral(f, contour, opts) | A Rect certain to contain the integral. Options tolerance (2⁻⁴⁰), order, bits, maxDepth, maxPieces. Refuses with singularity when f cannot be bounded somewhere on the contour. |

| residueSum(f, contour, opts) | The integral round a closed contour over 2πi. |

| argumentPrinciple(f, contour, opts), countZeros | The winding number of f(contour) round 0, a proven whole number: zeros minus poles inside. Refuses with zero-on-contour. |

| zeros(f, rect, opts) | { zeros: [{ enclosure, multiplicity, simple, isolating, boundary }], count, complete, unresolved }. Options bits (64), tolerance (2⁻²⁰), order, modelBits, maxCells. |

### Residues and real integrals

| Export | What it does |

| laurent(f, center, radius, { from, to }) | Laurent coefficients for the annulus holding the circle: coefficient(n), coefficients, principalPart, toString(). |

| residue(f, point, { radius }) | The residue at an exact point or an enclosure, a Rect. For text the circle is checked to hold no other zero of the denominator. |

| singularities(f, rect, opts) | For a formula as text: { singularities: [{ enclosure, kind, order, note }], complete, unresolved, numerator, denominator } with kind "pole", "removable", "essential", "branch point" or "undetermined". |

| realLineIntegral(f, { fourier, bits, variable }) | ∫ P/Q over the real line (times e^(iax) with fourier: a) by residues: { value, real, cos, sin, poles, steps }. |

| trigIntegral(f, { bits, variable }) | ∫₀^2π of a rational function of cos t and sin t: { value, real, poles, steps }. |

### Gamma and zeta

| Export | What it does |

| gamma(z, opts), rgamma(z, opts), logGamma(z, opts) | Γ(z), the entire 1/Γ(z), and log Γ(z) for Re z > 0 (the branch real on the positive axis). A point, Rect or Disc gives a Rect; a model gives a model. gamma refuses with pole at 0, −1, −2, … |

| zeta(s, opts), zetaTimesSMinus1(s, opts) | ζ(s), and the entire (s − 1)ζ(s). zeta refuses with pole at 1. |

| zetaZeros(t1, t2, opts) | The zeros of ζ with t1
| Export | What it does |

| quaternions, octonions, sedenions | The algebras of dimension 4, 8 and 16 over the rationals. |

| cayleyDickson(level, field) | The algebra of dimension 2level (level 0 to 8) over a field object, the rationals by default. |

| CayleyDickson | level dim name labels field zero one units; basis(i), of(...coefficients), parse(text), properties() → { commutative, associative, alternative, flexible, composition, zeroDivisors }. |

| quaternion(w, x, y, z), octonion(...c) | Elements from coordinates or text ("1 + 2i - k", "e1 + 2 e7"). |

| Hyper | An element: .coeffs, .algebra, .real, .imaginary; add sub mul neg scale conj norm inv pow rightDivide leftDivide commutator associator equals isZero. |

| QQ | The rationals as a field object. |

### @ratmath/complex/cayley: rotations

| Export | What it does |

| rotate(q, v) | The vector part of qvq−1, as three Rationals. |

| rotationMatrix(q) | The 3×3 rotation matrix as rows of Rationals. q need not have norm 1. |

| fromRotationMatrix(M) | The primitive quaternion of a rational rotation matrix; refuses a matrix that is not a rotation. |

| fromAxis(axis, t) | 1+t⋅axis: for a unit axis, t is the tangent of half the angle. |

| rotationOf(q) | { axis, cos, tanHalfSquared }, exact. |

| primitive(q) | The same rotation with whole-number coordinates sharing no factor, the first nonzero one positive. |

| interpolate(q0, q1, t) | (1−t)q0​+tq1​ the shorter way round: an exact rotation on the arc between them. |

### @ratmath/complex/cayley: integer quaternions

| Export | What it does |

| hurwitz(a, b, c, d) | A Hurwitz from coordinates that are all whole numbers or all halves of odd numbers, or from a quaternion. |

| Hurwitz | add sub mul neg conj equals isZero; norm() (BigInt); divmod(b) → { quotient, remainder } with this = quotient·b + remainder; isLipschitz, toIntegers(), toQuaternion(). The constructor takes doubled coordinates. |

| hurwitzUnits() | The 24 units. |

| hurwitzGcd(a, b) | A right greatest common divisor. |

| quaternionOfNorm(p) | A Lipschitz quaternion of norm p, for a prime p. |

| fourSquares(n) | Four BigInts, largest first, whose squares add to n. |

| fourSquaresCount(n) | The number of ordered, signed representations of n as four squares (Jacobi). |

### Try it

```js
// One of each.
const z = complex("3 + 4i");
PRINT("complex   ", z.toString(), " norm", z.norm().toString(), " sqrt", z.exactSqrt()[0].toString());
PRINT("rect      ", rect("1 + i", "1/10").mul(rect("2 - i", "1/10")).toString());
PRINT("disc      ", disc("1 + i", "1/10").inv().toString());
PRINT("polar     ", polar(z).exactModulus.toString(), "at", argument(z, 30).low.toNumber().toFixed(8), "rad");
PRINT("exp       ", exp(z, 80).toString(20));
PRINT("log       ", log(z).toString());
PRINT("log(-1)   ", log(-1).toString(6));
PRINT("root      ", root("-8", 3, { branch: 1, side: "above" }).toString(6), " (the real cube root of -8 is branch 1)");
PRINT("pow       ", pow("2", "1/2", 100).toString(25));
PRINT("asin      ", asin("1/2 + i").toString());
PRINT("continue  ", continueAlong("log", ["1", "i", "-1", "-i", "1"]).turns, "turn");
PRINT("winding   ", winding(["1", "i", "-1", "-i"]));
PRINT("quaternion", quaternion(1, 2, 3, 4).inv().toString());
PRINT("rotate    ", rotate("1 + i + j + k", [1, 2, 3]).join(", "));
PRINT("hurwitz   ", hurwitz(7, 3, -2, 5).divmod(hurwitz(2, 1, 1, 0)).remainder.toString());
PRINT("4 squares ", fourSquares(2026).join(", "));
Object.keys(octonions.properties())
```

Explore

## Explore

Type complex numbers and see what is exact, what is enclosed, and what happens on a branch cut. Further down: roots drawn in the plane, rotations by quaternions, Möbius maps, the zeros and poles of a function found with proof, and sums of four squares.

### Two numbers

zw

### A function of z

Function
Uncertainty ±
Bits

The function is applied to the z above. Give an uncertainty to turn z into a square of that half-width and watch the answer widen, or lie across a cut. Try the chips: each one sets z and a function at an interesting place.

### All the roots

nthe n-th roots of z, with the principal one marked

### A rotation

QuaternionVector

### A Möbius map

Sendto

Three points separated by semicolons, ∞ allowed. The picture shows where the lines Re z = −2, −3/2, …, 2 and Im z = −2, …, 2 go: each image is an exact circle or line.

### Zeros and poles in a rectangle

f(z)

Re from, toIm from, to

Every zero in the rectangle is isolated and proved: a filled dot is one simple zero, a ring is a zero of higher order with its order beside it, a cross is a pole. The count is checked a second way, by the argument principle on the boundary. See [Zeros and the argument principle](https://ratmath.com/complex/zeros.html) and [Residues](https://ratmath.com/complex/residues.html).

### Four squares

Whole number

### Try it

```js
// The page above, as code.
const z = complex("3 + 4i"), w = complex("1 - 2i");
PRINT("z·w =", z.mul(w).toString(), "  z/w =", z.div(w).toString(), "  |z| =", String(z.exactModulus()));
PRINT("log z =", log(z).toString());
PRINT("log of a square around -2:", log(rect("-2", "1/100")).toString(6));
PRINT("fifth roots of z:");
for (const r of roots(z, 5)) PRINT("   ", r.toString(10));
PRINT("rotate (1, 2, 3) by 1 + i + j + k:", rotate("1 + i + j + k", [1, 2, 3]).join(", "));
PRINT("zeros of exp(z) − 3z:", zeros("exp(z) - 3z", rect([-1, 3], [-2, 2])).zeros.map((z) => z.enclosure.toString(12)).join("  and  "));
fourSquares(2026)
```

Page: https://ratmath.com/complex/numbers.html

Complex rationals

## Complex rationals

A complex rational is a+bi with a and b fractions. They are closed under the four operations, so arithmetic on them is exact, with no rounding anywhere.

### Writing one

```js
import { complex, Complex } from "@ratmath/complex";

complex("3 - 4i");               // from text
complex(3, -4);                  // from two parts, each anything Core reads
complex(["1/2", "0.#3"]);        // 1/2 + 1/3 i
complex("(1 + 2i)/(3 - i)");     // text may be an expression: 1/10 + 7/10i
complex("(1 + i)^8");            // 16
complex(0.1);                    // 1/10: a decimal number means the decimal it prints as
```

Text is exact arithmetic on numbers in Core's notation (`1/2`, `0.25`, `0.#3` for a repeating decimal, `1..1/2` for a mixed number), the letter `i`, `+ - * /`, `^` with a whole-number exponent, and parentheses. `3/4i` reads as 43​i, the way it is written by hand.

### Arithmetic

```js
const z = complex("3 + 4i");
String(z.add("1 - i"));      // "4 + 3i"
String(z.mul("1/2 + i"));    // "-5/2 + 5i"
String(z.div("1 - 2i"));     // "-1 + 2i"
String(z.inv());             // "3/25 - 4/25i"
String(z.pow(-2));           // "-7/625 - 24/625i"
String(z.conj());            // "3 - 4i"
String(z.norm());            // "25": |z|², always rational
String(z.exactModulus());    // "5": |z| when it is rational, else null
z.equals("3 + 4i");          // true: equality is exact
```

Every method takes its argument in any of the forms `complex` reads. The parts are Core `Rational`s at `z.re` and `z.im`. Division by zero throws a `ComplexError` with `code: "division-by-zero"`.

### Why the norm and not the modulus

The modulus ∣z∣=a2+b2​ is usually irrational: ∣1+i∣=2​. Its square, the norm N(z)=zzˉ=a2+b2, is always rational and is multiplicative, N(zw)=N(z)N(w). So the exact layer works with the norm, and the modulus is an enclosure (see [Polar form](https://ratmath.com/complex/polar.html)) except when it happens to be rational, which is exactly when (a,b,∣z∣) is a rational Pythagorean triple.

### Exact square roots

Writing w=x+iy with w2=a+bi gives x2=(∣z∣+a)/2 and y2=(∣z∣−a)/2, with the sign of y that of b. So z​ is a complex rational exactly when ∣z∣ is rational and both of those are squares of rationals:

```js
complex("3 + 4i").exactSqrt().map(String);    // ["2 + i", "-2 - i"]
complex("-5 - 12i").exactSqrt().map(String);  // ["2 - 3i", "-2 + 3i"]
complex("-4").exactSqrt().map(String);        // ["2i", "-2i"]
complex("2").exactSqrt();                     // null: use sqrt() for an enclosure
```

### As a field

`CQ` is the field Q(i) as a RatMath field object (`add`, `mul`, `inv`, `zero`, `one` and the rest), which is what [linalg](https://ratmath.com/linalg/) matrices and [structures](https://ratmath.com/structures/) polynomials take when their entries are complex. Its `sign` is 0 for zero and 1 otherwise, because the complex numbers cannot be ordered: if i were positive or negative, i2=−1 would be positive.

### Try it

```js
// Gaussian rationals on the unit circle come from Pythagorean triples:
// (m + ni)² / (m² + n²) has modulus exactly 1.
const onCircle = (m, n) => complex(m, n).pow(2).scale(new Rational(1, m * m + n * n));
for (const [m, n] of [[2, 1], [3, 2], [4, 1], [5, 2]]) {
  const z = onCircle(m, n);
  PRINT(`(${m} + ${n}i)²/${m * m + n * n} = ${z}`, "  norm", z.norm().toString());
}

// Their products are again on the circle: rotations with no rounding, ever.
let w = complex(1);
for (let k = 0; k < 6; k++) w = w.mul(onCircle(2, 1));
PRINT("six of the first in a row:", w.toString(), "  norm", w.norm().toString());

// Exact roots, when there are some
for (const t of ["3 + 4i", "-5 - 12i", "5 + 12i", "2i", "1 + i"]) {
  const r = complex(t).exactSqrt();
  PRINT(`sqrt(${t}) =`, r ? r[0].toString() : "not a complex rational");
}

// The field object, as linalg would use it
CQ.format(CQ.div(CQ.from("1 + i"), CQ.from("1 - i")))
```
